correctness.rationale: Every prime p dividing n supplies a p-orbit of sigma^(n/p); its second-smallest point forces u congruent 1 mod p. The CRT least-significant-digit-first lexicographic order makes the earliest altered digit identical under t and ut whenever u congruent 1 modulo every p. Exact upper and lower hold for all n>=2. Finite checker independently matched all construction sizes 2..80 and exhaustively all cycles sizes 2..8.

originality.rationale: The full all-integer bound and squarefree-composite corollary are not stated in the inspected sources: the primary article proves rigidity only for prime lengths and acknowledges unrestricted composite collisions; the published reconstruction is only prime. The earlier prime-power theorem is expressly acknowledged as a covered subcase. Mixed-prime sharpness uses a single compatible CRT digit order and a prime-orbit obstruction. Bibliographic priority remains subject to independent checking.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical statement about identical orbit-comparison powers at composite lengths could be equivalent.
The prime-power restriction is already recorded and cannot count as independent novelty.
The assertion concerns powers only; it must not be confused with unrelated-cycle rigidity.
